schedule.subject: Why I changed the lighting in this cover-up
schedule.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

One of the cases in the guide is a samurai mask on the forearm. There was only a narrow strip of clean skin available for most of the highlights, so I built the design around it.

I chose a reference with rim lighting. That allowed most of the mask to stay in shadow, where the old tattoo could be covered, while preserving the sense of volume.

This is one reason a reference that looks perfect on paper may need to change before it becomes a cover-up.

See the before and after: https://vishartattoo.com/cover-up-tattoo-london/?utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=coverup_guide&utm_content=day3_samurai

Vladimir

schedule.subject: Another way to work with old tribal ink
schedule.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Here's a cover-up that isn't included in the guide: an old tribal tattoo on the chest, transformed into a wolf with a mountain landscape.

The finished composition has a different silhouette from the old design. The dark fur and mountain textures are part of a coherent image, rather than a flat block of black.

You can see it alongside the other before-and-after examples here: https://vishartattoo.com/cover-up-tattoo-london/?utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=coverup_guide&utm_content=day7_wolf

Vladimir

schedule.subject: Planning a cover-up? Here's what I need to see
schedule.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

If you're considering a cover-up, I can give you an initial assessment of the options.

Send me one clear close-up of the old tattoo, one wider photo showing where it sits, and a short description of what you'd like instead. Natural daylight and no filters are ideal.

I'll look at the existing pigment, the available space and whether a direct cover-up or a different approach makes sense.

Send photos here: https://vishartattoo.com/booking/?utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=coverup_guide&utm_content=day14_assessment

There's no obligation to book.

Vladimir Vishar
London
